entities.name: Abu al-Yusr al-Bazdawi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abu al-Yusr al-Bazdawi (c. 1030–1100), granted the honorific Sadr al-Islam, was a towering figure in Central Asian Islamic scholarship, specifically within the Hanafi school of jurisprudence and Maturidi theology during the late eleventh century. Operating primarily as a qadi (judge) in Samarqand, he was a pivotal intellectual force whose legal and theological acumen shaped generations of scholars, contributing significantly to the methodological consolidation of Islamic law. His work represents a crucial nexus where the practical application of law met sophisticated theological reasoning, making him indispensable to understanding the intellectual landscape of Transoxiana in the Seljuk era.

Bazdawi's most enduring contribution is his seminal work on the principles of Islamic jurisprudence, *Usul al-Bazdawi* (also known as *Kanz al-wusul ila ma'rifat al-usul*), which became a foundational textbook for the Hanafi school. This text meticulously delineated the sources and methodologies of legal reasoning, including Quran, Sunnah, ijma' (consensus), and qiyas (analogical reasoning), alongside the intricate process of istihsan (juristic preference) and 'urf (custom). Beyond his written legacy, Bazdawi was a renowned educator, whose students included luminaries like Najm al-Din 'Umar al-Nasafi, author of the widely studied creed *Aqida al-Nasafiyya*, and 'Ala' al-Din al-Samarqandi, further extending his intellectual lineage across the Islamic world.
